files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller's checklist

Owner: B. Okafor. Complete in sequence; no shortcuts.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, propose one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 and paying in July. If one exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; note that in some months every payroll run pays in-month.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and supporting contracts. Check the GL first to avoid a duplicate. If the entry is missing, book June amortization as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month a prepaid item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after first verifying what is already recorded in the GL.
5. Compare the June vendor-bill documents with the GL expense coding. Verify that each bill is in the correct expense account and reclass anything miscoded.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, only after items 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Anvil Works Manufacturing began in 2012 when two former plant-floor colleagues, a machinist and a production planner, started taking on small fabrication jobs from a rented workshop. Their early reputation came from fixing awkward, low-volume component problems that larger suppliers tended to decline. Over time, the company added machining, light assembly, finishing, and short-run production capabilities while keeping the practical, hands-on culture of the original shop.

Today, Anvil Works Manufacturing sells made-to-order brackets, housings, guards, fixtures, and compact assemblies to food processors, laboratory suppliers, technology firms, and other regional industrial customers. Work generally moves from customer drawing review through material preparation, fabrication, inspection, and shipment. The team includes experienced operators, a small engineering and estimating group, production coordinators, and an office staff that knows most customers by voice.

The company remains an ordinary going concern serving a steady mix of repeat accounts and project work. Its current focus is disciplined scheduling, dependable lead times, and cleaner handoffs between estimating, purchasing, production, and accounting. Management is also refining how the business presents itself in the market, with an emphasis on responsive service and the ability to handle specialized runs without making the process cumbersome for customers.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Position Anvil Works Manufacturing as the responsive, plain-spoken choice for specialized fabrication and short production runs. The message should emphasize practical engineering support, reliable communication, and parts built to customer specifications.

## Priorities

- Refresh the brand language and visual system without losing the shop-built character customers recognize.
- Publish concise capability stories showing how the team handles unusual drawings, tight handoffs, and repeatable production.
- Run two educational webinars per quarter for operations, sourcing, and engineering contacts.
- Pilot co-marketing with a complementary regional supplier.
- Improve follow-up materials for inquiries, quote requests, and dormant accounts.

## Content themes

Focus on manufacturability, material selection, inspection practices, short-run planning, and avoiding delays between design approval and production. Keep the tone useful rather than promotional; shop photos and operator commentary should do more work than generic claims.

## Channels

Use the company site as the primary destination, supported by email, professional social posts, webinar invitations, and partner referrals. Sales should receive short, reusable follow-up notes tied to each campaign theme.

## Quarter rhythm

In Q3, complete the messaging refresh, build the first capability stories, and launch the webinar cadence. In Q4, expand the strongest topics, test the partner pilot, and review lead quality with sales.

## Open items

Confirm internal owners, production availability for photography, and final spending after the Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# A few handoff notes

B. Okafor — a few things I learned the hard way:

- The bank slips its own fees and charges in near the end of the statement. We normally pick those up during close, not as they occur during the month, so do not overlook the last section.
- I was moving too fast in June, and the expense coding on one or two vendor bills may be wrong. Treat the source documents in `bills/` as authoritative and correct the GL to match them.
- The budget was locked early in Q2. None of the one-off June projects made it into the plan, and those items should account for most of the large budget variances.
- Payroll timing is the other catch: the back half of June pays in early July. The payroll register contains the actual dates, so use it for the accrual support.
